name: Stratum Executive Chrome-Panel Formal Suit
description:
Stratum's formal line for executive-tier employees is distinct from their standard corporate uniform output — this is a suit designed for representation, not function. Cut in a deep navy or charcoal wool-analog with a tight weave that reads as almost matte in daylight and slightly richer under interior lighting, the jacket features chrome-display panels along the upper lapels: small, polished insets that can be set to display a corponation logo, a tier-certification emblem, or left as mirror chrome. The panels connect to a small BCI-responsive module at the collar that allows the wearer to toggle display states with a thought. Augment-compatible shoulder and side seaming is standard.

This suit is what Stratum issues — or more precisely, what Stratum allows executives to purchase at a significant employee discount — when they need to represent the company at external events. It signals affiliation clearly and intentionally. The chrome panels catch the eye. That is the point. In rooms full of corporate formal wear, the display panel is a flag.
cultural_context: Seen at corponation partnership events, tier-ascension ceremonies, and inter-corporate diplomatic functions. The chrome panels make it immediately readable as Stratum-affiliated, which is either an asset or a liability depending on the room. Mid-level executives sometimes remove or cover the panels at personal events.
story_hooks: A character attends a neutral diplomatic function in this suit. The chrome panels displaying the Stratum logo create visible tension with the Arcturus delegation across the room. Someone asks them to turn the display off. They decline.
The BCI display module malfunctions and begins cycling through all available logos randomly. The wearer is in the middle of a negotiation and cannot stop it without visibly reaching for the override.

A former Stratum employee still owns this suit. They have not updated the logo display since leaving the company. At this point it reads as either a statement or an oversight, and they are no longer sure which.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, authoritative silhouette — tailored formal suit jacket and trousers with an understated luxury edge. The defining feature is the polished chrome display panels flanking the upper lapels, catching light like corporate insignia. Projects controlled ambition and institutional allegiance.
physical_description.fit: Precision tailored; fitted through the chest and waist with structured shoulders. Cut to accommodate augmented physiology without constraint. Clean lines, no excess fabric. The kind of fit that signals expensive tailoring.
physical_description.primary_material: Deep navy or charcoal wool-analog synthetic with a tight, high-quality weave. Matte in daylight, subtly lustrous under interior lighting. Durable, wrinkle-resistant, designed for climates without seasonal variation.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, densely woven fabric with a refined hand. The chrome panels are mirror-polished and cool to the touch. Collar features subtle BCI-module integration barely visible to the naked eye — a small circular dimple where the connectivity sits.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy or charcoal as primary. The chrome panels provide high-contrast metallic accents along the lapels. Interior lining typically corporate gray or navy. Minimal additional color — buttons are matte gunmetal.
physical_description.closures: Single-breasted button front with two or three matte gunmetal buttons. Magnetic closure option available on inner panels for augment access. Trousers feature standard zip and magnetic waistband closure.
distinctive_features: Polished chrome display panels on upper lapels — thought-responsive via BCI module
Can toggle between corporation logo, tier-certification emblem, or mirror chrome states
Augment-compatible shoulder and side seaming with discrete access points
Nearly invisible BCI receiver at collar — indicates high-end augmentation integration
Minimal branding — only subtle Stratum weave code visible in interior seam
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury presentation masking Tier 3-4 corporate identity. The suit itself costs significantly more than standard corporate wear, but availability is restricted to company employees.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn at corporate partnership events, tier-ascension ceremonies, inter-corporate diplomatic functions, and high-stakes corporate representation. The chrome panels are a deliberate signal of Stratum affiliation — a flag. Mid-level executives sometimes remove or cover panels at personal events to avoid constant institutional visibility.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine and meticulously maintained. Dry-cleaned regularly, chrome panels polished to mirror finish. The kind of garment that shows wear only after years of heavy rotation. When newer, shows almost no wrinkles.
